comparator.name: Philosophy
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 programme-specific EER and current student curriculum page establish a 180-EC, three-year Dutch-language Philosophy bachelor for students starting in 2026: a 120-EC major and 60 EC of profile space. The major comprises two compulsory first-year basic packages (60 EC), one required-choice deepening package (30 EC), two disciplinary compulsory courses (15 EC), Philosophy of Philosophy as the preparatory research seminar (7.5 EC), and the bachelor thesis (7.5 EC). The standard 7.5-EC thesis is used; the EER permits a 15-EC thesis only by individual agreement and by consuming 7.5 EC of profile space. The first-listed official deepening package, Ethics and Politics, is selected neutrally before considering UCR fit. Because the 2026 cohort reaches this package in academic year 2027–28, the odd-year alternate History of Political Philosophy is used rather than History of Ethics. The 60-EC profile space is represented as the required coherent 30-EC profile package plus 30 EC of remaining open profile space. All 180 EC are therefore accounted for without inventing electives.
components: Odd-academic-year alternate in the selected Ethics and Politics package; the 2026 cohort takes the package in 2027–28.

routeSelection.basis: The EER requires one of three 30-EC deepening packages and lists Ethics and Politics first. No target-specific evidence distinguishes a student's choice, so the first-listed package is used as a neutral tie-break before any UCR comparison. This route choice instantiates the comparator only; all three official directions remain separately assessed as programme-interest candidates.

Ethics, moral responsibility, political power, justice and social philosophy

Using philosophy to interpret contemporary social, scientific, technological and artistic problems

Language, mind and world as a focused direction in meaning, cognition and reality

alternatives.label: Philosophy, argument and historical perspectives
alternatives.concept: Builds the broadest available UCR philosophy pathway from ethics, mind, self, political philosophy, logic and persuasive reasoning, complemented by history, literature and cultural interpretation. It addresses Utrecht's cross-subdisciplinary core while remaining less philosophically specialised than the comparator.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines all five available UCR philosophy courses with political philosophy, logic, rhetoric, historical context and interpretive humanities, so its defining feature is breadth across philosophical questions, argument and historical perspectives.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters from Fall 2026 through Spring 2029. Personal & Professional Development is in Year 1; all course offerings match the fixed cohort terms; none of the selected courses has an unmet formal prerequisite; and eight level-3 courses are concentrated in Years 2 and 3 after introductory philosophy, politics, rhetoric, history and interpretive work.

alternatives.label: Ethics, politics, justice and institutions
alternatives.concept: Concentrates philosophical ethics and political thought around human rights, law, political institutions, social theory, conflict and public argument. This route turns Utrecht's Ethics and Politics package into a materially different UCR curriculum rather than merely relabelling the broad closest match.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme is dominated by ethics and political philosophy, human-rights and public-law study, political institutions, social theory, conflict and argumentative communication; the label names those sustained priorities rather than the external package alone.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces ten courses in archaeology, literary interpretation, intercultural history and general rhetoric with Law, Society & Justice, comparative politics, criminal and constitutional law, EU law, modern and contemporary sociology, environmental justice, gender history and an advanced history research seminar. The result prioritises normative public questions and institutions rather than a broad historical-philosophical survey.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters with Personal & Professional Development in Year 1. Law, Society & Justice is completed in the first semester before Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, Comparative Constitutional Law and Foundations of European Union Law. All offerings match the fixed cohort terms, and eight level-3 courses occur after introductory philosophy, politics, law and sociology.

alternatives.label: Mind, language, cognition and artificial intelligence
alternatives.concept: Develops Utrecht's Language, Mind and World direction through philosophy of mind, emotion, self and ethics, supported by logic, psycholinguistics, cognitive science, meaning, machine learning and AI ethics. The route studies representation and agency across philosophical, psychological and computational perspectives.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum clusters philosophy of mind, emotion and self with psycholinguistics, cognition, brain and behaviour, logic, meaning, machine learning and AI ethics; the final label states that interdisciplinary centre of gravity explicitly.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces twelve courses in political philosophy, law, history, archaeology, world literature and international politics with brain and behaviour, neurobiology, perception and action, psycholinguistics, social and experimental psychology, higher cognition, programming, machine learning, AI ethics and an advanced psychology research seminar. It therefore changes both the disciplinary mix and the central questions from broad philosophical history to mind, meaning and intelligent systems.
progression: The schedule uses six four-course semesters with Personal & Professional Development in Year 1. Introduction to Brain & Behavior is completed in semester 1 before Perception & Action, Psycholinguistics, Higher Order Functions and Advanced Research Seminar; introductory philosophy, rhetoric and brain science precede advanced mind, language and research work. All offerings match the fixed cohort terms, and seven level-3 courses occur in Years 2 and 3.

Mind, language, knowledge and human nature

Logic, cognitive science and research methods provide adjacent tools, but no selected UCR course directly reproduces Utrecht's combined epistemology and philosophy-of-science module.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics directly develops formal validity and symbolic reasoning from Logic and Language, while lacking the comparator's dedicated philosophy-of-language depth.
Research and interpretation courses support independent inquiry, but no selected UCR course reproduces Philosophy of Philosophy as a dedicated preparatory seminar.
No scheduled UCR course is a required 7.5-EC Philosophy bachelor thesis; the comparison separately displays optional independent research.

Utrecht reserves 30 EC for a coherent minor, second deepening package or approved study abroad; the fixed UCR alternatives are complete degree programmes rather than a direct one-to-one profile-space choice.
Utrecht's remaining 30 EC is open profile space, so no single scheduled UCR course is forced into an artificial comparator match.

selection.assessment: The closest match covers the broad cross-subdisciplinary Philosophy core. The first two official deepening-package directions, Ethics and Politics and Language, Mind and World, each produce a coherent and materially distinct 24-course UCR curriculum and are included as alternatives 2 and 3. The remaining official What Is the Human Being? direction is independently coherent and supported by philosophical anthropology, continental philosophy and identity interests, but the production contract permits at most three UCR alternatives; it is therefore recorded as maximum-reached rather than mischaracterised as incoherent or infeasible.

notes.text: Utrecht's 120-EC major provides a continuous Philosophy curriculum spanning history of philosophy, theoretical and practical subdisciplines, an advanced four-course deepening package, a preparatory research seminar and a required bachelor thesis. UCR offers five dedicated Philosophy courses and builds related routes with Politics, Law, Communication, History, Literature, Sociology, Cognitive Science, Psychology and AI. Those interdisciplinary combinations are defensible pathways but do not reproduce Utrecht's sustained specialist Philosophy depth, its advanced package as taught within one department, or its required Philosophy thesis.
